# Locations & Battles

## Avenue {#avenue}

The Avenue, also known as Spofford Avenue, is the finest residential street in [Kingsport](../codex/places.md#kingsport), lined with new and luxurious homes built by millionaires alongside a unique, quaint little cottage called Patty's Place.

> [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) drives the young girl through the Avenue and past local landmarks like Barry's pond as she chatters animatedly and renames the sights around them. She successfully guesses which house is [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), filling her with joy while [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) dreads the moment she learns the truth about the mistake.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) completes her second term at [Redmond](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) while navigating romantic attentions from [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and unwanted proposals from [Charlie Sloane](../character/charlie-sloane.md). Later, she and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) read a proposal from [Stella Maynard](../character/stella-maynard.md) to rent a house together for the next school year with Stella's [Aunt Jamesina](../character/aunt-jamesina.md) as housekeeper. After searching unsuccessfully all spring, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) spot a 'To Let' sign on Patty's Place along Spofford Avenue.
>
> — v3 · Chapter IX An Unwelcome Lover and a Welcome Friend

## Avonlea {#avonlea}

Avonlea is a rural community where [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), home to [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) and [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), and Lovers' Lane are located.

**Associated with:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Annetta Bell](../character/annetta-bell.md), [Barbara Shaw](../character/barbara-shaw.md), [Charlie Sloane](../character/charlie-sloane.md), [Elisha Wright](../character/elisha-wright.md), [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md), [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md), [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), [Stacy](../character/stacy.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) begins her first day teaching school, forgetting her prepared speech but managing her new pupils, including the sullen [Anthony Pye](../character/anthony-pye.md) and a bright, imaginative boy named [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md). After school, an excessively dressed Mrs. Donnell visits to demand specific pronunciations and names for her children. On her walk home, [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) gives [Anne](../character/anne.md) wild orchids, brightening her mood before she returns to recount her day to [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md).
>
> — v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) completes her school year and walks home, meeting young [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md) on her way to the Avonlea cemetery. They discuss their loved ones, imagination, and placing flowers on graves. At the cemetery, [Anne](../character/anne.md) meets Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md), and the two walk home together while discussing teaching, ideals, friendship, and future plans.
>
> — v2 · XV The Beginning of Vacation

> On [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) morning, [Diana](../character/diana.md) gives [Anne](../character/anne.md) a gift of dainty slippers sent by [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md). Later, the children perform in a successful [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) concert where [Anne](../character/anne.md) excels in her recitations, despite her initial nerves. Afterward, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) discuss Anne's performance by the kitchen fire and consider her future education.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) nervously visits Mr. [Harrison](../character/harrison.md) to confess that she accidentally sold his Jersey cow to Mr. [Shearer](../character/shearer.md). To her relief, Mr. [Harrison](../character/harrison.md) takes the mistake good-naturedly, accepts Anne's cow in exchange, and invites her to stay for tea. After sharing a pleasant conversation and bonding over cake and tea, [Anne](../character/anne.md) returns home to happily report the successful outcome to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md).
>
> — v2 · III Mr. Harrison at Home

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) spends an evening in the garden with [Ruby](../character/ruby-gillis.md), who tearfully confesses her fear of dying and her desire to go on living. Shortly after [Anne](../character/anne.md) leaves, [Ruby](../character/ruby-gillis.md) passes away peacefully in her sleep. Following the funeral, [Anne](../character/anne.md) reflects on life and death while walking home with [Diana](../character/diana.md) and [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md).
>
> — v3 · Chapter XIV The Summons

## Bailey {#bailey}

The old Bailey place is an abandoned, ruined house and garden near [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) that is rumored to be haunted by the ghost of [Henry Warren](../character/henry-warren.md).

## Beechwood {#beechwood}

Beechwood is the residence of [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md), located in town, where [Anne](../character/anne.md) stays while taking her [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) exams.

**Associated with:** [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md)

> [Diana](../character/diana.md) meets [Anne](../character/anne.md) in Lover's Lane to share the news that her [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md) has invited them both to [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown) for the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition). After getting permission to go, the girls travel to Beechwood, Aunt Josephine's estate, where they enjoy several days of town festivities, concerts, and dining out. After returning home, [Anne](../character/anne.md) reflects warmly on the trip and her joy at returning to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life

## Bingen {#bingen}

Bingen is a location on the [Rhine](../codex/places.md#rhine) referenced in the title of a poem recited by [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and known by heart by [Anne](../character/anne.md).

## Birch Path {#birch-path}

Named by [Diana](../character/diana.md), the Birch Path is a narrow, scenic woodland trail fringed with white birches and wild flora that runs through Mr. Bell's woods to the main road, serving as part of [Anne](../character/anne.md) and Diana's picturesque route to school.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) walk to school while discussing their classmates, including [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) Blythe's return. During class, [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) teases [Anne](../character/anne.md) by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' prompting [Anne](../character/anne.md) to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. [Phillips](../character/phillips.md) punishes [Anne](../character/anne.md) by making her stand in front of the class, and she refuses to forgive [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) afterward.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. [Anne](../character/anne.md) proposes starting a story club to cultivate their imaginations, which eventually expands to include other classmates like Jane and [Ruby](../character/ruby-gillis.md). Later, [Anne](../character/anne.md) talks with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) about the story club's progress, defending their work and sharing her aspirations to be like Mrs. [Allan](../character/allan.md) before [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) prompts her to finish her household chores.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed

> On the evening before school opens, [Anne](../character/anne.md), Jane, and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) debate their teaching methods and views on corporal punishment at a crossroads. [Anne](../character/anne.md) then walks back through her favorite spots, avoids Mrs. Lynde's unsolicited advice at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), and visits Mr. [Harrison](../character/harrison.md), who also doubts her plan to rule without whipping. The next morning, a nervous [Anne](../character/anne.md) is comforted by [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) as she prepares for her first day as a teacher.
>
> — v2 · IV Different Opinions

## Bolingbroke {#bolingbroke}

Bolingbroke is a place in [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) where both [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md) were born.

**Associated with:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) spends a pleasant two weeks visiting [Phil](../character/phil-gordon.md) Gordon's homestead in Bolingbroke while being courted by Phil's suitors. She visits her childhood home and meets the current owner, who gives her a packet of old love letters written by her deceased parents. After visiting her parents' graves in the cemetery, [Anne](../character/anne.md) returns to read the letters, feeling deeply connected to her mother and father at last.
>
> — v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday

## Boston {#boston}

Boston is a noisy, crowded big city where [Jordan](../character/jordan.md) Gray worked for a winter, meeting his wife [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Murray while she was working in a store, and to which he later returned after her death.

**Associated with:** [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md)

## Bright River {#bright-river}

Bright River is a location eight miles from [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), featuring a train station house with a long platform and a small hotel with a yard.

> [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) travels to the Bright River train station expecting to pick up an orphan boy, but instead finds an imaginative, talkative young girl waiting for him. Learning from the stationmaster that there has been a mistake, [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) decides to take her home to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to let [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) handle the situation. As they drive away together in the buggy, the young girl chatters enthusiastically about her life, her wild imaginations, and her distress over her red hair.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised

## Camelot {#camelot}

Camelot is a romantic, historical setting featured in Tennyson's poetry, which [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) envies for its old-fashioned romance and incorporates into a dramatic game with her friends.

## Canada {#canada}

Canada is a nation governed from Ottawa whose political affairs are a frequent topic of debate among electors like Mrs. [Lynde](../character/lynde.md).

## Carmody {#carmody}

Carmody is a nearby town with a school where [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md) was appointed to teach, and it features shops that locals visit via a road connected to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), [Newbridge](../codex/places.md#newbridge), and [White Sands](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel).

**Associated with:** [Joshua Pye](../character/joshua-pye.md), [Morgan](../character/morgan.md), [Shearer](../character/shearer.md)

## Charlottetown {#charlottetown}

Charlottetown is a location on Prince [Edward Island](../codex/places.md#edward-island) accessible by train, featuring notable red roads, train connection from a boat landing point, and employment opportunities that runaways seek out.

**Associated with:** [Allan](../character/allan.md), [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md), [Miss Barry](../character/miss-barry.md), [Perry](../character/perry.md)

## Columbia {#columbia}

Columbia, also referred to as St. Columbia, is a location with an educational institution where [Jonas](../character/jonas.md) [Blake](../character/blake.md) studies theology.

**Associated with:** [Jonas](../character/jonas.md)

## Convocation {#convocation}

Convocation is the college ceremony held following examinations at [Redmond](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) where graduates are capped, gowned, and awarded their diplomas by the university president.

## Crystal Lake {#crystal-lake}

Crystal Lake is a name suggested by Jane for a boggy pool, which was chosen by lot when she, [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) named the spot during their outing.

## Dryad’s Bubble {#dryad-s-bubble}

The Dryad's Bubble is the name given by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/di.md) to a spring located down by the log bridge, surrounded by ferns and birch trees near the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood).

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) share a tearful, romantic farewell after Mrs. [Barry](../character/barry.md) forbids [Diana](../character/diana.md) from playing with [Anne](../character/anne.md). Consoled by their devotion and a exchanged lock of hair, [Anne](../character/anne.md) decides to return to school, where she is warmly welcomed back by her classmates and receives a secret note of friendship from [Diana](../character/diana.md). She dedicates herself to her studies, engaging in an intense academic rivalry with [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) while maintaining her silence toward him.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) plans a spring outing with [Diana](../character/diana.md), [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md), and Jane to celebrate an adopted spring birthday. During their walk through the woods and pastures, the girls explore unknown paths, name a woodland pool, and discover [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's forgotten garden, where [Diana](../character/diana.md) tells the romantic story of Hester's life.
>
> — v2 · XIII A Golden Picnic

> After helping [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) with his evening prayers, [Anne](../character/anne.md) walks down to Dryad's Bubble where she meets [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md). They discuss the progress of the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society) and their upcoming school term before [Anne](../character/anne.md) returns home to talk with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) about her plans for the next day.
>
> — v2 · XIX Just a Happy Day

## East Grafton {#east-grafton}

East Grafton is a location where Miss [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) traveled to visit a seriously ill distant relative.

**Associated with:** [Baxter](../character/baxter.md)

## Echo Lodge {#echo-lodge}

Echo Lodge is a stone house inhabited by Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md) the [Fourth](../character/fourth.md) that serves as the setting for consultations and preparations leading up to Miss Lavendar's wedding.

**Associated with:** [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) returns to teaching, dealing with schoolhouse antics and comforting [Dora](../character/dora.md) after [Mirabel Cotton](../character/mirabel-cotton.md) scares her with stories of her deceased relatives. Later, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) take a walk through the woods and accidentally lose their way while heading to a tea party. Their wrong turn leads them to Echo Lodge, where they meet the eccentric Miss [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and her young maid, [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md) the [Fourth](../character/fourth.md), who invite them to stay for a pretend tea party.
>
> — v2 · XXI Sweet Miss Lavendar

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) enjoy tea with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and her young servant, [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md) the [Fourth](../character/fourth.md), in her house and garden. Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) demonstrates the garden's magical echoes and explains how all her young helpers ended up named [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md). Before the girls leave, [Anne](../character/anne.md) accidentally mentions [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md), which briefly brings a subtle change and quiet sadness over Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) as they say goodbye.
>
> — v2 · XXI Sweet Miss Lavendar

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) walks to Echo Lodge to visit Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md), and they spend an enjoyable evening sharing stories, tea, and candy. Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) opens up about her past romance and broken engagement with [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md), prompting [Anne](../character/anne.md) to suggest bringing his son, [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md), for a visit. A month later, [Anne](../character/anne.md) introduces [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) to Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md), and the two quickly form a warm and fond connection.
>
> — v2 · XXIII Miss Lavendar’s Romance

> During dinner, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) asks [Anne](../character/anne.md) about her outfit and shares stories from school while [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) tries to keep him in line. Afterward, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) walk to Echo Lodge to visit Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md) the [Fourth](../character/fourth.md). While [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) plays with the echoes and talks about his grandmother's strict rules, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) chat before [Anne](../character/anne.md) goes strawberry picking with [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md).
>
> — v2 · XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House

> [Charlotta](../character/charlotta.md) the [Fourth](../character/fourth.md) confides her worries about Miss Lavendar's melancholy behavior to [Anne](../character/anne.md), leading [Anne](../character/anne.md) to promise to return for a extended visit to cheer her up. After a outdoors tea with strawberries, Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) sits with [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) in the garden and shares stories about her imaginary dream-boy, which resonates deeply with Paul's own imagination before [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) head home.
>
> — v2 · XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House

## Eden {#eden}

Eden is a biblical garden referenced metaphorically to describe a perfect, idyllic paradise.

## Edward Island {#edward-island}

Edward Island, also referred to as Prince Edward Island, is a region where custom dictates that travelers nod to everyone they meet on the road.

## England {#england}

England is a distant location mentioned by [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) as a place far enough from the [Island](../codex/places.md#island) that adopting a child from there might yield someone quite different from local residents.

**Associated with:** [John Selwyn](../character/john-selwyn.md)

## Entrance {#entrance}

The Entrance is an examination taken by advanced students to qualify for admission into Queen's.

**Participants:** [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md)

## Europe {#europe}

Europe is an overseas destination where Miss [Patty](../character/patty.md) and [Maria](../character/maria.md) Spofford travel for a multi-year trip, and a region that Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md) postponed visiting to attend Anne's wedding.

## Exhibition {#exhibition}

The Exhibition is an event held in [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown) to which [Aunt Josephine](../character/aunt-josephine.md) invited [Diana](../character/diana.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md) to visit and stay with her at [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood).

**Participants:** [Harmon Andrews](../character/harmon-andrews.md), [Josie Pye](../character/josie-pye.md), [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md)

## Four Winds {#four-winds}

Four Winds is a coastal region features a harbor, channel, red sandstone cliffs, sand dunes, and a lighthouse situated on a cliff spur jutting out into the gulf.

**Associated with:** [Frank West](../character/frank-west.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) are welcomed to their new home at Four Winds by [Doctor Dave](../character/doctor-dave.md), his wife, and Captain Jim. They enjoy a lively supper together while learning about their surrounding neighbors and the local community.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) walk to Four Winds Light in the evening, encountering the strangely bearded [Marshall Elliott](../character/marshall.md) along the way. At the lighthouse, Captain Jim warmly welcomes them, showing them his model schooner, the mechanism of the light, and his orange cat, the [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md). Over tea and a driftwood fire, Captain Jim explains [Marshall](../character/marshall.md) Elliott's political vow and shares stories of his past and saved animals.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) walks through a foggy evening to visit [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md), but turns back after seeing [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) weeping intensely in private. Outside, she meets Captain Jim leading [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md) home; Captain Jim then walks [Anne](../character/anne.md) back to her house while they discuss [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and Dick's tragic situation.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 13 A GHOSTLY EVENING

> As spring arrives at Four Winds, Captain Jim visits [Anne](../character/anne.md) to decorate her garden beds with shells and bring her sweet-grass and mayflowers. Miss Cornelia and Captain Jim engage in lively, humorous debates about religion, books, and local neighbors alongside [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md). When [Susan Baker](../character/susan.md) returns with news about a sick neighbor, her unconscious funny remark causes Captain Jim and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to step outside to laugh.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 18 SPRING DAYS

> [Cornelia](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) brings writer [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md) to Anne's home so [Anne](../character/anne.md) can guide him to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) Moore's house, where he will be boarding. During their walk, Owen expresses his connection to the area through his grandfather [John Selwyn](../character/john-selwyn.md) and confides his hope to write a great Canadian novel. Upon arriving, Owen is struck by Leslie's striking beauty and is warmly introduced into her household.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES

## Four Winds Harbor {#four-winds-harbor}

Four Winds Harbor is a body of water featuring an old wharf and a channel through which ships, such as the Royal William, sail to reach the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) and surrounding shore.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) drive together through the picturesque scenery toward their new home at Four Winds Harbor. Along the way, [Anne](../character/anne.md) admires the landscape and notices a remarkably beautiful girl driving geese near a starkly neat house. They finally arrive at their new house, where [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) welcomes [Anne](../character/anne.md) across the threshold.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 5 THE HOME COMING

> Captain Jim and [Anne](../character/anne.md) bond over their shared nature as "kindred spirits," or people who belong to the race that knows [Joseph](../character/joseph.md). As the guests prepare to leave in the moonlight, Captain Jim shares stories and praises the beauty of [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds). After everyone departs, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) walk through their garden, grateful for their happy home.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) reflect on their happy honeymoon month at Four Winds Harbor and Gilbert's successful emergency medical case. Later, Miss Cornelia [Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) arrives to call on [Anne](../character/anne.md), bringing her sewing and offering her sharp, frank opinions on men, local neighbors, and church denomination differences while [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) listens in from the office.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 8 MISS CORNELIA BRYANT COMES TO CALL

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) goes for a evening walk on the shore of Four Winds Harbor and encounters [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md), her mysterious neighbor. They share a conversation about their surroundings, beauty, and pasts before agreeing to exchange visits. Returning home, [Anne](../character/anne.md) discusses her encounter and impressions of [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) with [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md).
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) spend autumn evenings visiting Captain Jim at the lighthouse, often accompanied by [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md). On their walk home, they discuss Leslie's wasted potential before turning to affectionate teaseing about Anne's past suitor and their shared joy in their own home.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 14 NOVEMBER DAYS

## Four Winds Point {#four-winds-point}

Four Winds Point is a coastal location featuring a lighthouse kept by Captain Jim, situated near sand dunes and a harbor halfway from [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) walk to the Four Winds Point lighthouse to ring in the [New Year](../codex/places.md#new-year) with Captain Jim, his nephew Joe, [Marshall Elliott](../character/marshall.md), and the [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md). After music, dancing, and storytelling around the fire, Captain Jim opens the door at midnight to welcome the [New Year](../codex/places.md#new-year).
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT

> [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) drives [Anne](../character/anne.md) to Four Winds Point to sit outdoors, leaving her with Captain Jim while he sees a patient. Sitting among the rocks, Captain Jim comforts [Anne](../character/anne.md) regarding her lost baby Joyce and shares the tragic story of his long-lost love, [Margaret](../character/margaret.md). He asks [Anne](../character/anne.md) to remember [Margaret](../character/margaret.md) and pass her story on to future generations so she won't be forgotten.
>
> — v4 · CHAPTER 20 LOST MARGARET

## Germany {#germany}

Germany is a country ruled by a Kaiser, from which a travelling peddler sought to bring his wife and children.

## Glen {#glen}

The Glen is a valley town containing a lending library, a [Presbyterian](../codex/factions.md#presbyterian) manse, and a surrounding area overlooked by hills, a marsh, and the [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley).

**Associated with:** [Hammond](../character/hammond.md), [Henry](../character/henry.md), [Perry](../character/perry.md), [Susan](../character/susan.md)

> [Faith](../character/faith.md) walks down the Glen with [Walter](../character/walter.md), who suffers from a toothache and worries about his inability to confront bullies like [Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md), who hurls insults at [Faith](../character/faith.md) as they pass. [Faith](../character/faith.md) then visits [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) to persuade him to return to church and pay his salary, but she is initially intimidated and retreats after he shouts at her. Furious at his insults, [Faith](../character/faith.md) returns to confront him directly; impressed by her fiery spirit, Norman apologizes, agrees to return to church, and invites her to sit for supper.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT

When she arrives, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) reveals that Mr. Meredith proposed to her, but [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) strictly refuses to release [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) from her vow not to marry, despite Rosemary's pleas. [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) subsequently writes a cold refusal letter to [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md), leaving both Meredith and [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) heartbroken while [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) tries to justify keeping her sister to herself.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXII. ST. GEORGE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT

> [Jerry](../character/jerry.md) decrees punishments for the children's cowardice, sending [Carl](../character/carl.md) to sit in the graveyard until midnight. [Carl](../character/carl.md) bravely endures the cold, rainy vigil, but falls dangerously ill with double pneumonia as a result. After a grim fight for his life, [Carl](../character/carl.md) recovers with the support of the family and community, and the children celebrate his return to health.

Green Gables is the secluded, meticulously kept [Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) family homestead in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), featuring a big, rambling house situated at the far edge of their cleared land at the end of a long, grassy lane.

Later, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) discovers the brooch caught in her own lace shawl, apologizes to [Anne](../character/anne.md), and quickly sends her off to enjoy the picnic.

## Harbour Head {#harbour-head}

Harbour Head is a local community near [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary and [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), home to the Hill sisters and the wealthy, touchy Mrs. [Alec Davis](../character/davis.md).

**Associated with:** [Davis](../character/davis.md)

## Haunted Wood {#haunted-wood}

The Haunted Wood is a gloomy spruce grove located over the brook that [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) imaginatively populated with romantic ghosts, including a wailing white lady, a murdered child's ghost near [Idlewild](../codex/places.md#idlewild), a headless man, and skeletons.

## Havana {#havana}

Havana is a port destination reached by the vessel the *[Four Sisters](../codex/tech.md#four-sisters)* to discharge and take on cargo, where [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md) was later discovered by Captain Jim in a sailors' boarding house after suffering a severe head injury.

## Hell {#hell}

Hell, also referred to as the other place, is an awful location where the devil resides and where bad people who break the [Sabbath](../codex/places.md#sabbath) or do not do good are said to burn in fire forever after they die.

## Hopeton {#hopeton}

Hopetown is a location home to an asylum authority responsible for placing orphan home children.

## Idlewild {#idlewild}

Idlewild is the poetical name invented by [Anne](../character/anne.md) for the playhouse she and [Diana](../character/diana.md) set up in a ring of white birch trees on Mr. William Bell's land.

## Ingleside {#ingleside}

Ingleside is the residence of the [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) family, located near a big maple grove, a valley, and the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary pond.

**Associated with:** [Susan](../character/susan.md)

> [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) approaches Ingleside while [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Susan Baker](../character/susan.md) sit on the veranda chatting after Anne's return from [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe). [Susan](../character/susan.md) watches over six-year-old [Rilla](../character/rilla-blythe.md) and baby [Shirley](../character/shirley.md) while recounting recent local gossip to [Anne](../character/anne.md), including an incident involving Mrs. Harrison Miller.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER I. HOME AGAIN

[Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) finishes her knitting and runs down to [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), where she tells [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) about Mrs. [Alec Davis](../character/davis.md) leaving the church and the potential loss of ministry salary. Horrified at the thought of having to move away from [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary, [Faith](../character/faith.md) decides she must act to convince [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) to return to the congregation.

## Island {#island}

The Island is a region located close to [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), where local residents contrast its native-born populace with those from places such as [Hopeton](../codex/places.md#hopeton), [England](../codex/places.md#england), or the [States](../codex/places.md#states).

**Associated with:** [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Harrison](../character/harrison.md), [Morgan](../character/morgan.md), [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md)

## Japan {#japan}

Japan is a foreign country where [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) resides with her husband, and a destination visited by the Ford family to gather material for a novel with a Japanese setting.

Kingsport is a university town featuring a historical harbor bay and an old tree-lined cemetery containing the grave of an eighteen-year-old midshipman killed during an 1813 naval conflict between the Shannon and the Chesapeake.

There they meet [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md), a friendly and talkative fellow student from [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia). The three girls strike up an instant friendship while sitting on a gravestone, sharing their mutual feelings of homesickness and experiences on their first day.

After discovering an old war grave in the cemetery that deeply moves [Anne](../character/anne.md), the trio parts ways. [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) then discuss Phil's lively character, agreeing that despite her frivolity, they genuinely like her.

## London {#london}

London is a place from which Miss Patty's brother [Aaron](../character/aaron.md) brought a pair of century-old china dogs fifty years ago, and it is also associated with homeless "street Arabs" whom [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) refused to adopt.

## Lover {#lover}

Lover's Lane is a romantic pathway opening below the [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) orchard, extending into the woods to the end of the [Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) farm, which [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) use as part of their scenic walk to school.

## Lowbridge {#lowbridge}

Lowbridge is a nearby place connected by road where the Corey family, known for their good looks, originated.

**Associated with:** [Myra Murray](../character/myra-murray.md)

## Lynde’s Hollow {#lynde-s-hollow}

Lynde’s Hollow is a depression where the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) main road dips down, featuring a home, an orchard, a quiet brook fringed with alders and ladies’ eardrops, and a view of the steep red hill road leading out of the peninsula.

## Marysville {#marysville}

Marysville is a place where Mr. and Mrs. [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md) moved after leaving [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), and where [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) lived and briefly attended school until she was eight years old.

## Maywater {#maywater}

Maywater is the former home of the Meredith family before they moved to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), where they previously attended church and were acquaintance with local figures such as Mrs. Johnson and Mr. Isaac Crothers.

**Associated with:** [Faith](../character/faith.md)

## Merry Christmas {#merry-christmas}

The event refers to [Anne](../character/anne.md) and Gilbert's first Christmas together in their [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) home, marked by a bright, fine day, a snowy landscape, and a feast attended by visiting friends and relatives including [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md), the twins, Captain Jim, and Miss Cornelia.

## Methodist Church {#methodist-church}

The Methodist Church is a local place of worship whose congregation Deacon Warren belongs to, and which features a graveyard adjacent to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary manse.

## Millersville {#millersville}

Millersville is a settlement notable for its homely schoolma'ams, where William Obadiah goes to court a woman and [Sam](../character/sam.md) considers renting a place of his own.

## Montreal {#montreal}

Montreal is a city home to doctors and a surgeon consulted by [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) regarding an operation to restore [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md).

## Morley {#morley}

Morley Andrews is a student at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school who was punished by [Anne](../character/anne.md) for driving trained crickets in the aisle during class.

## Mount Holly {#mount-holly}

Mount Holly is the beautiful, old Gordon homestead in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), where [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md) lives and hosts gay gatherings for her friends.

**Associated with:** [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md)

## New Brunswick {#new-brunswick}

New Brunswick is a region where [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) visited his cousins over the summer and the location of a tragic incident in which an adopted girl poisoned her family's well.

**Associated with:** [Harrison](../character/harrison.md), [James A](../character/james-a.md), [Wiley](../character/wiley.md)

## New Year {#new-year}

The arrival of the New Year was marked by [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), [Marshall Elliott](../character/marshall.md), and Captain Jim opening the lighthouse door at midnight after spending the final hours of the old year together, observing the rare shadow of [Venus](../codex/places.md#venus) in the snow on their way to the [Four Winds Point](../codex/places.md#four-winds-point).

## Newbridge {#newbridge}

Newbridge is a bustling little village connected by road to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), known for its residents naming a tree-arched stretch of road "the [Avenue](../codex/places.md#avenue)" and home to political agent [Jerry Corcoran](../character/jerry.md).

**Associated with:** [Annetta Bell](../character/annetta-bell.md), [Jerry](../character/jerry.md)

## Nova Scotia {#nova-scotia}

Nova Scotia is a Canadian region home to an orphan asylum, situated close to Prince [Edward Island](../codex/places.md#edward-island).

**Associated with:** [George](../character/george.md), [George Moore](../character/george-moore.md)

Orchard Slope is the home of [Diana Barry](../character/di.md) and her family, featuring a house with a western gable located up through a brook and the firs from [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables).

## Pacific {#pacific}

The Pacific coast is a destination that Mr. and Mrs. [Irving](../character/irving.md) visit on a trip following their late August wedding.

Patterson Street is a street located in a slum area where the Reverend Jo [Blake](../character/blake.md) takes a position at a small mission church and settles down with his wife, [Phil](../character/phil-gordon.md).

## Rainbow Valley {#rainbow-valley}

Rainbow Valley is a secluded, romantic valley featuring wild cherry trees, spruce, mossy paths, and a brook running through it, situated behind the maple grove near [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside) and [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary.

> [The Blythe](../codex/factions.md#the-blythe) children gather in Rainbow Valley, their favorite play area behind the maple grove. [Jem](../character/jem.md) cooks freshly caught trout over a campfire while the siblings chat about their surroundings, flying dreams, and their love for the place. Just as they prepare to eat their meal, an unexpected visitor arrives from the direction of the manse.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN

> [The Meredith](../codex/factions.md#the-meredith) children sit in the old [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) graveyard chatting about town gossips, buried people, and their new [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) neighbors. Drawn by a wonderful smell, they run down into Rainbow Valley and join the [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) children for a meal of trout. The two groups quickly become firm friends as they share stories of their lives.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN

> Miss Cornelia investigates Mary's past and learns that Mrs. [Wiley](../character/wiley.md) has died, leaving Mary an orphan once more. Meanwhile, the children gather in Rainbow Valley to hear [Walter](../character/walter.md) read myths and share stories. [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md) arrives with the news of Mrs. Wiley's death, startling Mary, while [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) promises to pray that Mary can remain in [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds).
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES

> Mary joins the children in Rainbow Valley and informs [Faith](../character/faith.md) and [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) that they have caused a scandal by mistakenly cleaning house on Sunday. The children realize [Faith](../character/faith.md) lost track of the days because prayer meeting was moved. Afterwards, [Walter](../character/walter.md) describes his poetic vision of heaven to the group, and [Faith](../character/faith.md) assures [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) that she has a plan to clear up the town's misunderstanding.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY

> Mr. Meredith observes his children during supper and reflects on Mrs. Davis's complaints about their behavior. Seeing that Mrs. [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) is away, he decides to visit the [West](../character/west.md) homestead to return a borrowed book and enjoy the company of [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) and [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md).
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ALEC DAVIS MAKES A CALL

## Redmond College {#redmond-college}

Redmond College is a higher education institution where students pursue a four-year Arts course with subjects such as English, Classics, Mathematics, dead languages, and geometry, culminating in final examinations, [Convocation](../codex/places.md#convocation), and a graduation dance.

**Associated with:** [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Blythe](../character/blythe.md), [Charlie Sloane](../character/charlie-sloane.md), [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), [Jonas](../character/jonas.md), [Margaret](../character/margaret.md), [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md), [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md), [Roy Gardner](../character/roy-gardner.md), [Stella Maynard](../character/stella-maynard.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) settle into college life at Redmond, finding themselves drawn into social circles through their friendship with [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md). [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) earns distinction among the Freshmen after leading them to victory in the annual Arts Rush. Anne's homesickness is relieved when she receives a collection of letters from her friends and family back home in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).
>
> — v3 · Chapter V Letters from Home

## Rhine {#rhine}

The Rhine is a location mentioned in the poem "[Bingen](../codex/places.md#bingen) on the Rhine," which [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) has memorized and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) recites at a concert.

## Rome {#rome}

Rome is a famous city whose construction [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) notes was not accomplished in a single day.

## Sabbath {#sabbath}

The Sabbath is a sacred day, commonly referred to as Sunday, dedicated to attending church or [Sunday School](../codex/places.md#sunday-school), learning theology and Bible verses, and abstaining from work or worldly pastimes like fishing.

## Shining Waters {#shining-waters}

The Lake of Shining Waters is a long, winding body of water—locally known as Barry's pond—spanned by a bridge and surrounded by sand-hills, marshland, and groves of fir and maple.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), and Jane plead with [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, but he refuses. Later, [Anne](../character/anne.md) accidentally overhears Judson taking a political bribe from [Jerry Corcoran](../character/jerry.md) near the Lake of Shining Waters. Fearing [Anne](../character/anne.md) will expose his corruption and ruin his reputation, Judson agrees to cancel the ad deal to keep her quiet, though [Anne](../character/anne.md) refuses to make a deal and simply keeps the secret out of principle.
>
> — v2 · XIV A Danger Averted

## Snow Queen {#snow-queen}

The Snow Queen is the name given by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) to the exceptionally white, blooming cherry tree located outside her bedroom window.

## Spain {#spain}

Spain is a place associated with the imaginary, glittering castles that [Anne](../character/anne.md) shapes out of the mists and rainbows of her lively fancy while daydreaming by the fire.

## Spencervale {#spencervale}

Spencervale is a town situated ten miles from [Carmody](../codex/places.md#carmody), featuring farm properties and a quiet, green highway known as the [Tory Road](../codex/places.md#tory-road).

**Associated with:** [Chester Ross](../character/chester-ross.md), [Mary](../character/mary.md)

## States {#states}

The States, also known as the United States, is a foreign country where [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md) went into business with his uncle, married, and raised his ten-year-old son, [Paul](../character/paul-irving.md), before sending him to live with his grandmother in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea).

**Associated with:** [Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md)

## Summerside {#summerside}

Summerside is a town where [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) spent three pleasant years teaching prior to her marriage.

## Sunday School {#sunday-school}

Sunday School is a religious class that [Faith](../character/faith.md) and [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) attempted to attend on a rainy day, only to find the building empty because they had lost track of the days and mistaken Saturday for Sunday.

## Thanksgiving {#thanksgiving}

Thanksgiving is an annual holiday celebrated in November, though [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) mused that it would be far better celebrated in May when nature is alive and flowering.

## The Morgan {#the-morgan}

Located in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), the [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) place is a large, comfortable house featuring grounds with a big lawn, ancient trees, a twelve-acre hardwood grove, a fine orchard, a storybook-like garden enclosed by a high brick wall, and a view of the harbor, dunes, and lighthouse.

## Toronto {#toronto}

Toronto is a place where Mrs. Charlotte E. [Morgan](../character/morgan.md), the clever author of "Edgewood Days" and "The Rosebud Garden," resides.

## Tory Road {#tory-road}

Tory Road is a quiet, little-traveled green highway in [Spencervale](../codex/places.md#spencervale) lined with young spruces, built by the [Tory](../codex/factions.md#conservative) government and home to the [Copp](../character/copp.md) girls and [Martin](../character/martin.md) Bovyer.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) apologizes to Miss [Sarah](../character/sarah.md) [Copp](../character/copp.md) for looking into her pantry, and the two negotiate the purchase of the willow-ware platter. Miss [Sarah](../character/sarah.md) treats [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) to tea and bread while sharing the news that she is getting married. After successfully securing the platter, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) drive home along the Tory Road, reflecting on their adventurous day.
>
> — v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road

## Valley Road {#valley-road}

Valley Road is a community situated two miles from its train station, known for having good-looking schoolteachers and operating a school with a July and August summer term.

**Associated with:** [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md)

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) arrives at Valley Road station and gets a ride to her boarding house with Mrs. Amelia [Skinner](../character/skinner.md), who is filling in on the mail route for her new husband. During the drive, Mrs. [Skinner](../character/skinner.md) entertains [Anne](../character/anne.md) with stories about choosing true love over wealth and warns her about local geography before dropping her off at [Wayside](../codex/places.md#wayside).
>
> — v3 · Chapter XXX Mrs. Skinner’s Romance

> [Janet](../character/janet.md) takes [Anne](../character/anne.md) to a prayer meeting in Valley Road, where they meet [John Douglas](../character/john-douglas.md), who walks [Janet](../character/janet.md) home. Later, John invites [Janet](../character/janet.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md) to his house for tea to meet his mother, who acts excessively sweet and fragile while subtly making [Janet](../character/janet.md) uncomfortable. [Anne](../character/anne.md) notices John's pained expression during the visit and wonders about the true dynamic in his household as they return to [Wayside](../codex/places.md#wayside).
>
> — v3 · Chapter XXXII Tea with Mrs. Douglas

## Vancouver {#vancouver}

Vancouver is a place mentioned both as the new residence of a dear friend of [Aunt Jamesina](../character/aunt-jamesina.md) and as one of the far-flung locations where a fictional minister's wife buried a child in a story written by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md).

## Venus {#venus}

Venus is a brilliant, golden evening star and earth-sister celestial body that, when drawn near to Earth, can cast a faint, mysterious shadow on white snow that is visible only with averted vision.

## Victoria Island {#victoria-island}

Victoria Island is a ravishing spot discovered by [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) up the brook, featuring two maple trees and surrounded by the flowing brook, which they named in honor of finding it on the Queen's birthday.

## Violet Vale {#violet-vale}

Violet Vale is a green dimple in the shadow of Mr. Andrew Bell's woods, named by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), that sits along the scenic route she and [Diana Barry](../character/di.md) take to school and is said to be filled with millions of violets in the spring.

## Wayside {#wayside}

Located in a hollow in [Valley Road](../codex/places.md#valley-road), Wayside is the small, picturesque home of Miss [Janet](../character/janet.md) Sweet, featuring an orchard and flower garden in front, a mossy roof, and a path near a dangerous marsh.

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) writes a letter to [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md) describing her new life as a schoolteacher at [Valley Road](../codex/places.md#valley-road), boarding with Miss [Janet](../character/janet.md) Sweet at Wayside. She describes her cozy accommodations, Janet's cooking, and an awkward visit from the neighbor's hired boy, [Sam](../character/sam.md). [Anne](../character/anne.md) also hints at an ongoing elderly romance in the area, though she vows not to interfere after a past mishap.
>
> — v3 · Chapter XXXI Anne to Philippa

> [Anne](../character/anne.md) receives an awkward proposal from [Sam](../character/sam.md), which she politely rejects and later laughs about with [Janet](../character/janet.md). Shortly after, [Alec](../character/alec.md) arrives to announce that John Douglas's mother is dying, and she passes away soon after. Following the funeral, [John Douglas](../character/john-douglas.md) comes to Wayside and proposes to [Janet](../character/janet.md), explaining that his late mother had forced him to swear a secret oath not to marry while she was alive.
>
> — v3 · Chapter XXXIV John Douglas Speaks at Last

## White Lady {#white-lady}

The "White Lady" is a young, exceptionally straight silver birch tree growing by the brook in the favourite hollow of [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), named by [Walter Blythe](../character/walter.md).

## White Sands Hotel {#white-sands-hotel}

The White Sands Hotel is a large establishment run by Mr. Kirke along the shore, popular with [American](../codex/factions.md#american) tourists visiting for the summer season.

**Associated with:** [Blewett](../character/blewett.md), [John Henry Carter](../character/john-henry-carter.md)

> [Diana](../character/diana.md) helps [Anne](../character/anne.md) dress for a concert performance at the White Sands Hotel, where [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) offers her usual blunt observations before [Anne](../character/anne.md) leaves with [Diana](../character/diana.md), Jane, and [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md). Upon arriving at the grand hotel, [Anne](../character/anne.md) experiences intense stage fright while waiting among sophisticated performers and audience members. However, after spotting [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) in the crowd, her pride kicks in, allowing her to deliver a brilliant recitation that wins over the audience and earns her high praise.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert

## White Way {#white-way}

The White Way of Delight is the imaginative name given by [Anne](../character/anne.md) to a wonderful, wonderfully beautiful place known locally as the [Avenue](../codex/places.md#avenue).

## Willowmere {#willowmere}

Willowmere is a scenic location situated past Mr. Barry's back field along the romantic route that [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) walk to school.
